title: Personal Credit Cards: APR cap and fee relief while the customer is on active military duty
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: military active-duty rate cap

This policy covers the military rate cap on the Personal Credit Cards line: when it applies, what it changes on the account, how interest billed above the cap is reversed, and what happens when active duty ends. The cap percentage is the tier's own term.

## Policy clauses

1. While the customer's military status on the customer profile is active duty:
   - every APR on the account is capped at the tier's active-duty APR cap;
   - the account is repriced with the military rate cap in effect;
   - the penalty APR is suspended;
   - no annual fee is billed.
2. Interest billed above the cap for any cycle after the military status became active duty is reversed for the excess, on the military benefit ground.
3. The military rate cap applies only while the customer's military status on the profile is active duty.
4. When active duty ends, the cap is removed and the pre-cap APRs return on the first statement after the change.
5. The cap never raises an APR that is already below it.

## Evidence

The status that counts is the military status recorded on the customer profile in the bank's records. A statement by the customer alone does not switch the cap on or off.

## Effect card

| Item on the account | While active duty is on the profile | After active duty ends |
|---|---|---|
| APRs above the cap | held at the cap | pre-cap APRs return on the first statement after the change |
| APRs already below the cap | unchanged | unchanged |
| Penalty APR | suspended | the suspension under this policy ends |
| Annual fee | not billed | this policy no longer excludes it |
| Interest already billed above the cap for a cycle after active duty began | excess reversed on the military benefit ground | not applicable |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical accounts)

- An account carrying an introductory balance transfer APR of 0.00% keeps that APR; the cap never raises an APR.
- The reversal covers only the excess above the cap, not the whole interest charge.
- A cycle that ended before the military status became active duty is not a cycle after that change, so it is outside the excess reversal.
